about.title: Chico Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Chico is a town people move through on foot, on bikes, and behind the wheel, and with roughly 90,000 residents sharing the Esplanade, SR-99, Cohasset Road, and East Avenue, collisions happen more often than anyone would like. In 2025, public records show 209 injury collisions in Chico, leaving 258 people hurt and three families grieving. Those reports cluster on Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when commuters, students, and shoppers are all trying to get home at once. If you were one of the people injured, you probably have questions about medical bills, a totaled car, and the adjuster who keeps calling. LawProactive exists to answer the first one: who should I talk to? We are not a law firm. We are a free service that matches you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles Chico car accident claims on a contingency basis, so you owe nothing unless your case results in a recovery. Reach out, describe what happened, and let a professional carry the paperwork while you focus on healing.

whyChoose.title: Why Chico Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Your deadline is closer than it looks
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, but a claim against a city, county, or state agency can require notice in as little as six months. Getting connected early keeps every option open.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still pursue compensation even if you shared some of the blame for a crash on East Avenue or Cohasset Road. Your recovery is simply reduced by your share of responsibility.

items.title: Free to connect, contingency to represent
items.desc: LawProactive charges nothing to match you with an attorney, and network attorneys work on contingency. If there is no recovery, there is no attorney fee.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other insurer a recorded statement, and it is generally wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can shrink your claim later. Politely say you will be in touch after you get advice, then let us connect you with someone who can handle that conversation for you.

items.question: I was hit on SR-99 near Chico and a Caltrans or city vehicle was involved. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It can change your timeline significantly. When a government entity may be responsible, California typically requires a formal claim to be filed within six months, far shorter than the usual two-year window. Because of that, it is important to speak with an attorney quickly rather than waiting for the insurance process to play out.

items.question: What should I do in the first few days after a Chico car accident?
items.answer: Get medical care even if you feel mostly fine, since neck and back symptoms often show up later. Save photos, dashcam footage, the police report number, and the names of any witnesses, and keep every bill and receipt. Preserving that evidence early gives whichever attorney you work with far more to build on.
